newsitem.title: LEBANON: Signs of compromise in Lebanon labour split.
newsitem.headline: Signs of compromise in Lebanon labour split.

text.p: Signs of a possible solution to a bitter split in Lebanon's labour movement emerged on Friday after pro-government union leaders sought mediation to resolve their dispute with arrested leftist leader Elias Abou Rizk.

An envoy of the International Labour Organisation also arrived in Beirut amid reports that he would try to heal the rift opened in April by the election of rival pro- and anti-government leaderships to the General Labour Confederation (CGTL).
Supporters of pro-government leader Ghneim al-Zoghbi asked journalists' union chief Melhem Karam on Thursday to help work out a reconciliation between the two groups.

Beirut newspapers said the release on Wednesday after questioning of a second unionist, Yasser Nehme, and the decision of a magistrate not to charge him and Abou Rizk with denigrating Lebanon's reputation abroad indicated that the authorities might be backing down.

Abou Rizk's May 30 arrest on charges of falsely claiming to head the CGTL has brought widespread protests and a demand by Amnesty International for his release. Amnesty called the fiery, 54-year-old unionist a prisoner of conscience.
An opposition committee of unionist, politicians and intellectuals in support of Abou Rizk said on Thursday it had decided to call a general strike and demonstrations to demand his release.

Nehme said after his release that Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri had taken a "personal interest" in his case. Newspapers said Hariri intervened with the judiciary to obtain his release but this could not be independently confirmed.

Abou Rizk, who was seeking re-election to a second four-year term as CGTL chief in the April 24 elections, harried Hariri during his first term with a series of general strikes and attempted demonstrations to demand better conditions for workers whom he said had been forgotten by the government.
Abou Rizk's campaign gained wide support from the political opposition and he came close to obtaining election to parliament on a leftwing ticket in general elections last summer.
